title: Dominant affine chart and generic germ comparison
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of integral schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme] with dense image. Write $\eta_X,\eta_Y$ for the generic points [def-sc-generic-point] and $k(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}$, $k(Y)=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$ for the function fields [def-sc-function-field]. Let $V\subseteq Y$ be a nonempty affine open whose inverse image $U=f^{-1}V$ is affine. Set $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Y)$, $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be pullback of sections [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then $f(\eta_X)=\eta_Y$, the points $\eta_Y,\eta_X$ belong to $V,U$, their primes in $A,B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] are $(0)$, and $A,B$ are domains. The generic germ maps $j_A:A\to k(Y)$, $j_B:B\to k(X)$ are injective and exhibit those fields as fields of fractions: every element is a quotient of two such germs with nonzero denominator. The map $\varphi$ is injective. With $\alpha:k(Y)\to k(X)$ the canonical generic stalk map [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map], one has $j_B\varphi=\alpha j_A$ and
$$\alpha(j_A(a)/j_A(a'))=j_B(\varphi(a))/j_B(\varphi(a'))\qquad(a,a'\in A,\ a'\ne0).$$
Put $\mathcal F(W)=\Gamma(f^{-1}W,\mathcal O_X)$ for each open $W\subseteq Y$, and $C=\mathcal F_{\eta_Y}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $\iota:B\to C$ be the germ map, $\sigma:k(Y)\to C$ the stalk of $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal F$, and $c:C\to k(X)$ the ring map sending a germ over $f^{-1}W$ to its germ at $\eta_X$. These are well defined and satisfy
$$c\iota=j_B,\qquad \sigma j_A=\iota\varphi,\qquad c\sigma=\alpha.$$
In particular $\sigma(j_A(a)/j_A(a'))=\iota(\varphi(a))\iota(\varphi(a'))^{-1}$ for $a'\ne0$. No finiteness, Noetherianity, normality or dimension hypothesis is imposed, and no bijectivity of $c$ is asserted.
